procedure.description: targeted genomic sequence analysis panel, solid organ neoplasm, 51 or more genes

denial.carcText: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer.
denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 81455 (targeted genomic sequence analysis panel, solid organ neoplasm, 51 or more genes) with date of service 2026-04-26. CARC 56: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer. RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: Panels of more than 50 genes are investigational under the plan’s genetic testing policy and are not covered.

criteria.text: Multi-gene next-generation sequencing panels of more than 50 genes are considered investigational for solid tumors under this plan and are not covered; single-gene or small-panel testing is the covered alternative.
Recurrent, relapsed, refractory, metastatic, or advanced stage III or IV cancer.
The patient is seeking further cancer treatment and the result will inform the selection of therapy.
The same tumor panel has not previously been performed for this primary cancer.

The panel is an FDA-approved or cleared companion diagnostic, or its use is recommended by National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines for the tumor type (RAS, BRAF, HER2, microsatellite instability, and NTRK status for metastatic colorectal cancer).

chart.text: Blood pressure check. 119 over 87 today, 124 over 88 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.1, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Vitamin D came back 19. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 196, LDL 126, HDL 59, triglycerides 148. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Sigmoid colon biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. Mismatch repair proteins intact by immunohistochemistry.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
CT chest, abdomen, pelvis with contrast: circumferential sigmoid mass with regional nodes, 2 hepatic lesions in the right lobe, largest 2.6 centimeters, consistent with metastases. No lung lesions.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

75 year old man in medical oncology after colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia found a sigmoid mass. Long conversation about what stage IV means and what treatment looks like. He is realistic and motivated. ECOG 1. Port referral placed. His history otherwise: migraines, rare now, osteoarthritis of the hands, hypertension on lisinopril. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 12 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Stage IV sigmoid adenocarcinoma with synchronous liver metastases. He wants treatment. Results will determine whether he is a candidate for anti-EGFR antibody therapy, BRAF-directed therapy, HER2-directed therapy, or immunotherapy, and the chemotherapy backbone will start while we wait. No prior molecular testing on this tumor; the biopsy block is available at pathology. Ordering the solid tumor next-generation sequencing panel to cover KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, HER2 amplification, microsatellite status, and NTRK fusions in one assay, per NCCN for metastatic colorectal cancer.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
A1c came back 6.4. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.

Back to start treatment. Panel sent to the reference laboratory today from the biopsy block. FOLFOX cycle 1 scheduled for next week; we will adjust the biologic once the molecular results are back. Vitals today 128 over 86, pulse 78.

expected.note: Plan exclusion: crit-1 (coverage) cannot be met by any chart content.
